title: Benchmark Guardian: CI baselines & automated perf-gating
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: We currently lack a deterministic, automated CI gate that detects performance regressions (tokens/sec drop, p95 latency increase) for the serving runtime. Intermittent regressions slip through because PRs rely on ad-hoc manual runs, and our baselines are scattered across spreadsheets.

Goal: Implement a reproducible CI-level benchmark guardian that: (1) runs a standardized micro-benchmark on PRs that touch runtime or kernel selection code, (2) compares results to a maintained baseline, (3) fails the PR if the regression exceeds statistical and business thresholds, and (4) produces artifacts and dashboards for triage. The system must be robust to noise from infra variability and fast enough to be practical in PR flows.

Key metrics & thresholds (proposal):
- tokens/sec: baseline determined per model/config; fail if median tokens/sec drops by >5% relative to baseline AND p-value < 0.05 from bootstrapped comparison.
- p95 latency: fail if p95 increases by >3% relative to baseline with similar statistical check.
- Minimum confidence: run n=5 independent benchmark trials and use the median; require 3/5 trials consistent to flag a regression.

Baseline storage: persistent baseline catalog in S3 (s3://redwood-perf-baselines/serving/) and a simple metadata CSV/JSON that maps model+config -> baseline values and last validation commit. Baselines are auto-updated from green CI runs on main following the rolling-window policy (last 30 green builds).

Implementation POC: a Buildkite job "perf/ci-gate" that pulls the perf-harness binary, runs the workload on a dedicated GPU perf worker (label: gpu-perf), uploads artifacts (raw traces, token counts, latency histograms) to S3, and posts a structured check to GitHub with pass/fail and links to artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: A Buildkite CI job (perf/ci-gate) exists and is runnable from PRs that touch runtime or perf-critical files.
The job runs a canonical workload (single model + representative prompt set) with defined warm-up, KV priming, and collection of tokens/sec and latency histograms.
Results are compared against the canonical baseline for that model/config; the job marks the GitHub check as failed when thresholds are exceeded.
Artifacts (raw samples, histograms, runner logs) are uploaded to S3 and linked from the GitHub check for triage.
A dashboard tile in Console (perf-regressions) shows recent CI comparisons and the rolling baseline metadata.
Documentation exists (Confluence) describing how to run locally, how baselines are updated, and troubleshooting steps for noisy failures.
steps: Design canonical workload and measurement protocol (warm-up 50 ops, 512-token seq, batch sizes 1 and 8), include KV cache priming sequence.
Implement harness runner changes in perf-harness repo: deterministic seeds, fixed model checkpoint reference, use identical tokenization and batching code paths as runtime.
Create Buildkite job 'perf/ci-gate' with gpu-perf runner and secure access to baseline S3 bucket.
Add statistical comparator library (bootstrap CI) and threshold logic to gate step; allow override via PR comment for infra flakiness investigations.
Wire artifact upload and GitHub status check with structured summary (metrics table + artifact links).
Add baseline catalog schema (JSON) and updater job on main that refreshes baseline when main CI is green (rolling window retention = 30).
Create Console dashboard tile for CI-perf comparisons and hook alerting to #perf-alerts Slack channel for persistent regressions.
